name: Shaphan (scribe under Josiah)
title: King's scribe and law mediator
summary: Shaphan was a royal scribe under King Josiah of Judah. He played a crucial role in the religious reformation when he received the Book of the Law found in the temple and read it aloud to the king. His family continued to serve in important positions and supported the prophet Jeremiah.

keyEvents.title: Sent to inspect the temple work
keyEvents.description: King Josiah sent Shaphan to the high priest Hilkiah to supervise the temple repairs and the money collected for the work.

keyEvents.title: Received the Book of the Law from Hilkiah
keyEvents.description: Hilkiah handed over the Book of the Law that had been found in the temple to Shaphan, who read it and brought it to the king.

keyEvents.title: Read the Book of the Law to King Josiah
keyEvents.description: Shaphan read the Book of the Law aloud to the king, which caused Josiah to tear his clothes in grief and repentance over the people's disobedience.

keyEvents.title: Sent to the prophetess Huldah
keyEvents.description: Shaphan was among those the king sent to inquire of the Lord through the prophetess Huldah regarding the words in the Book of the Law.

keyEvents.title: Parallel account in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: The same event concerning the discovery of the Book of the Law and Shaphan's role is also recorded in 2 Chronicles.
